description: Sutra governance hooks — collapsed to the sutra-turn runtime (W0a). One `sutra-turn run --event <E>` registration per event the pipeline declares with at least one step (six today) plus the bare sutra-canary at UserPromptSubmit — seven entries; the pre-collapse registry is kept verbatim at hooks/hooks.json.step3 and is what runtime/pipeline.json is derived from and judged against. NO EMPTY EVENTS ARE REGISTERED: UserPromptExpansion was registered here while the pipeline declared zero steps for it and hooks.json.step3 carried no such registration at all, i.e. the fleet fires nothing on that path today; every prompt expansion would have forked sutra-turn only to select no step, write an orphan_turn + stage_digest row and exit — pure overhead and a new failure surface on a path that has none. It is dropped from this registry AND from the pipeline; runtime/spec-check.sh check 13 now fails the release gate, naming the event, if an event is declared with zero steps or if a `sutra-turn run --event <E>` registration exists for an event the pipeline does not declare with at least one step. TIMEOUTS ARE DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN: the timeout on each registration is ceil(max(pipeline.events[<E>][].timeout_ms)/1000) + 5 s of runtime margin. Before the collapse each slow hook carried its own host timeout, so only that hook was killed; under one registration per event the host SIGKILLs sutra-turn at the event cap and the whole event is lost (no step rows, no emit, no stage_digest — only the orphan_turn row). runtime/spec-check.sh check 12 asserts, per event, that this timeout*1000 is >= the largest step timeout_ms in the pipeline and that budgets.event_wall_ms is too, so a step budget can never again be raised past its host cap unnoticed.
